headline: Acquisition fuels sales surge as net income slips
summary_short: Q2 net sales surged 92% y/y to $1,566M on the newly acquired Allison Off-Highway business, but net income fell 7% to $181M and diluted EPS dropped 6% to $2.15 on acquisition-related costs and higher interest expense.
summary_long: Net sales grew primarily from the Allison Off-Highway acquisition ($706M contribution), while the legacy Allison Transmission business grew 6% to a record $860M on Defense and North American truck demand. Consolidated gross margin held near 33%, but net income fell y/y on higher SG&A, D&A, and interest expense tied to acquisition financing, plus mark-to-market losses on marketable securities. Adjusted EBITDA rose 29% to $404M and adjusted diluted EPS grew 8% to $2.73, excluding acquisition-related items. Cash fell to $399M and long-term debt rose to $4,094M following the acquisition, though the company repaid $150M on its revolver and repurchased $46M of stock. Allison raised full-year 2026 guidance across revenue, EBITDA, net income, operating cash flow, and free cash flow.

drivers.explanation: Consolidated results were reshaped by the Allison Off-Highway acquisition, which drove the sales surge and EBITDA growth but also added D&A, interest expense, and one-time integration costs that pulled GAAP net income down y/y.

Net sales rose on the addition of the Allison Off-Highway business ($706M), while the legacy Allison Transmission unit grew 6% to a record $860M on Defense end-market growth and North American truck market momentum.
Gross profit growth was principally driven by the addition of the Allison Off-Highway business unit.
Consolidated cost of sales rose almost entirely from including the newly acquired Off-Highway segment's $588M cost of sales this quarter, which has no year-ago comparable.

Decrease was driven by higher operating costs (including increased D&A) from the Off-Highway acquisition, plus higher net interest expense and unrealized mark-to-market losses on marketable securities.
Cash fell mainly on the $2,529M net cash outlay for the Off-Highway acquisition, partly offset by new debt and financing inflows raised to fund it.
Debt rose y/y to fund the Off-Highway acquisition; within the quarter the company reduced debt by repaying the remaining $150M outstanding on its revolving credit facility.
